$comment: Reproducible fixture for the representative instrument matrix (openspec/changes/build-market-data-hub/tasks.md 3.1). Contains only public, factual identifiers (ISIN, ticker, MIC/venue) taken from public sources; it contains no credentials or personal data. 'figi' is deliberately left null: it SHALL be resolved at runtime via OpenFIGI's DiscoveryPort (see openfigi-evaluation.md) rather than being fixed here as a value unverified by this review.

instruments.name: SAP SE
instruments.raw_close_semantics: Xetra closing-auction price published by Deutsche Börse; no dividend/split adjustment is applied to the retained 'close' value (specs/market-observations).
instruments.expected_historical_range: Has traded on Xetra since well before the start of any candidate source evaluated; in practice the recoverable range depends on each source's historical depth (e.g. the Deutsche Börse Public Dataset PDS only covers from 2018 onward).
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: Xetra weekends and holidays (FWB/Xetra calendar, e.g. Christmas, New Year, Good Friday); no session on 24 and 31 December in years when they fall on a weekday, per the calendar published by Deutsche Börse.
instruments.relevant_quotas: See source_decisions.json: deutsche_boerse_public_dataset (commercial NO-GO), alpha_vantage_free (25 req/day), twelvedata_free (8 req/min, 800/day).
known_anomalies: The Deutsche Börse PDS aggregates into 1-minute bars and does not directly publish an official EOD 'close': the close must be derived from the last bar of the session.
German equities can undergo splits or denomination changes (e.g. WKN changes); the raw close is not adjusted retroactively in the MVP.

instruments.name: Siemens AG
instruments.expected_historical_range: Historical quotation predates any candidate source by a wide margin; the recoverable range is limited by each source, not by the instrument.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: Same Xetra holiday calendar as sap-se-xetr.
instruments.relevant_quotas: See source_decisions.json: same candidate sources as sap-se-xetr.
known_anomalies: Siemens has undergone historical corporate spin-offs (e.g. Siemens Energy, Siemens Healthineers) that are not reflected in the raw 'close' and are not adjusted for in the MVP (out of scope, see design.md § Risks/Trade-offs).

instruments.name: LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE
instruments.raw_close_semantics: Euronext Paris official closing price (the 'closing price' from the closing-auction mechanism); raw, unadjusted 'close'.
instruments.expected_historical_range: Historical quotation predates any candidate source evaluated by a wide margin.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: Weekends and holidays of the Euronext calendar (shared across XPAR/XAMS/XBRU/XLIS with occasional local variations).
instruments.relevant_quotas: See source_decisions.json: euronext_eod_datashop (UNRESOLVED, requires an EMDA for redistribution).
known_anomalies: Euronext operates several national markets (XPAR, XAMS, XBRU, XLIS) under one group but with slightly different local holiday calendars; do not assume a single Euronext calendar.

instruments.name: ASML Holding N.V.
instruments.raw_close_semantics: Euronext Amsterdam official closing price; raw, unadjusted 'close'.
instruments.expected_historical_range: Historical quotation predates any candidate source evaluated by a wide margin.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: Euronext Amsterdam (XAMS) holiday calendar, which differs on specific dates from XPAR's.
known_anomalies: ASML also trades on Nasdaq (ADR/listing in USD); a provider identifier can confuse the EUR line on XAMS with the USD line on Nasdaq if not filtered by MIC and currency (see specs/instrument-catalog § 'Ambiguous EUR match').

instruments.name: iShares Core MSCI World UCITS ETF USD (Acc)
instruments.raw_close_semantics: Xetra closing price for the EUR quotation line of a UCITS ETF domiciled in Ireland; raw, unadjusted 'close'. Note: the quotation currency (EUR on Xetra) is independent of the fund's base currency (USD).
instruments.expected_historical_range: The ETF was registered on 25/09/2009 per its own documents; the EUNL line on Xetra may have an admission date different from the fund's creation date.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: Xetra holiday calendar; additionally, an ETF may go untraded on a given day for lack of liquidity without that day being a holiday (a market-driven missing session, not a source-driven one).
instruments.relevant_quotas: See source_decisions.json: same candidate sources as the Xetra equities.
known_anomalies: The same ISIN (IE00B4L5Y983) trades under different tickers depending on the market (e.g. SWDA on the London Stock Exchange, EUNL on Xetra): specs/instrument-catalog § 'ISIN with multiple quotations' applies directly to this ISIN.
It is an accumulating (Acc) ETF: it does not distribute visible cash dividends, which can be mistaken for the absence of corporate events when comparing price series.

instruments.name: Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF USD (Acc)
instruments.raw_close_semantics: Xetra closing price for the EUR quotation line; raw, unadjusted 'close'.
instruments.expected_historical_range: ETF launch date: 23/07/2019 per the issuer's documents; the actually recoverable range depends on the source.
instruments.relevant_quotas: See source_decisions.json: same candidate sources as the Xetra equities.
known_anomalies: A physically replicating ETF with multiple quotation lines across different markets/currencies; requires explicit resolution by MIC+currency, same as ishares-core-msci-world-eur-xetr.

instruments.name: Amundi Funds Euro Corporate Bond - A EUR (sub-fund of the Amundi Funds SICAV)
instruments.venue: N/A (not exchange-listed; subscription/redemption at NAV through Amundi Luxembourg SA, the UCITS Management Company, domiciled in Luxembourg)
instruments.raw_close_semantics: There is no market 'close': the relevant daily observation is the NAV (Net Asset Value) per share, treated as the raw EOD 'close' for this asset class (specs/operations § differentiated calendars; design.md § 'Different strategies by frequency').
instruments.expected_historical_range: The sub-fund and share class (A) launched on 1 February 1999 per the official KIID in force as of 9 June 2022; the recoverable NAV history in practice depends on whether the management company publishes full series since launch or only a recent period.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: The KIID states that shares are subscribed/redeemed 'on any dealing day' per the prospectus; days that are not dealing days (Luxembourg holidays and the fund's own calendar) publish no NAV. The 'WAITING_FOR_PUBLICATION' status (specs/market-observations) applies while the day's NAV has not yet been published.
instruments.relevant_quotas: No candidate source evaluated in this wave generically, freely, and with clear permissions covers the NAV of non-listed Amundi UCITS funds; see price-providers-evaluation.md. amundi.com itself publishes the 'latest net asset value' but was not evaluated as a third-party candidate source in this wave.
known_anomalies: The sub-fund has several share classes with distinct ISINs for the same strategy (e.g. (A) LU0119099819 accumulating and (D) LU0119100179 distributing, per the KIID); resolve by the exact ISIN of the class, not just by the sub-fund's name.

No MIC or exchange ticker: the catalog must admit these fields as absent without fabricating them, the same way it already admits the absence of ISIN/MIC for crypto assets (specs/instrument-catalog § 'Crypto asset without ISIN or MIC').

instruments.name: Amundi Funds Euro Government Bond - A EUR (sub-fund of the Amundi Funds SICAV)
instruments.venue: N/A (not exchange-listed; subscription/redemption at NAV through Amundi Luxembourg SA, the UCITS Management Company, domiciled in Luxembourg)
instruments.raw_close_semantics: There is no market 'close': the relevant daily observation is the NAV (Net Asset Value) per share, treated as the raw EOD 'close' for this asset class (specs/operations § differentiated calendars; design.md § 'Different strategies by frequency').
instruments.expected_historical_range: The sub-fund and share class (A) launched on 1 July 2010 per the official KIID in force as of 11 February 2022; the recoverable NAV history in practice depends on whether the management company publishes full series since launch or only a recent period.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: Same dealing-day pattern as amundi-funds-euro-corporate-bond-a-eur: days without a NAV coincide with Luxembourg holidays and the fund's own calendar, not with the calendar of any regulated market.
instruments.relevant_quotas: Same candidate sources (or lack thereof) as amundi-funds-euro-corporate-bond-a-eur: none generically covers the NAV of this fund with clear permissions.
known_anomalies: The sub-fund has several share classes with distinct ISINs (e.g. (A) LU0518421895 accumulating and (D) LU0518421978 distributing, per the KIID); resolve by the exact ISIN of the class.
No MIC or exchange ticker, the same optional-field pattern as amundi-funds-euro-corporate-bond-a-eur and as the crypto assets without ISIN/MIC.

instruments.name: Bitcoin / Euro
instruments.venue: Crypto spot market (e.g. Kraken, Bitstamp; the exact venue depends on the adapter and SHALL be recorded as provenance)
instruments.raw_close_semantics: No regulated market close: EOD 'close' is defined by MarketRelay's own convention as the last price of the UTC 24/7 session (e.g. 00:00 UTC), treated as raw with no adjustment (splits/dividends do not apply to crypto).
instruments.expected_historical_range: Depends on the chosen venue; large centralized exchanges typically cover several years of BTC/EUR history.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: In theory none (24/7 market); in practice gaps can occur due to exchange maintenance or source outages, which SHALL be treated as a source-missing session, not a market-missing session (specs/market-data-ingestion).
instruments.relevant_quotas: See source_decisions.json: coingecko_free_demo (redistribution NO-GO), kraken_public_rest_api (UNRESOLVED), bitstamp_public_rest_api (UNRESOLVED).
known_anomalies: The BTC/EUR price can differ by several basis points between exchanges due to liquidity fragmentation: specs/market-observations § 'Two approved sources disagree' applies directly.
The definition of a 'daily UTC session' (e.g. cutoff at 00:00 UTC) is a MarketRelay convention, not a market standard; it must be documented and kept stable so as not to break historical series.

instruments.name: Ether / Euro
instruments.venue: Crypto spot market (e.g. Kraken, Bitstamp; the exact venue depends on the adapter and SHALL be recorded as provenance)
instruments.expected_historical_range: Depends on the venue; generally somewhat shorter than BTC/EUR since it is a younger asset.
instruments.expected_missing_sessions: Same as btc-eur-spot: in theory none, in practice gaps due to source incidents.
known_anomalies: Network events (e.g. hard forks, consensus-mechanism changes) can produce anomalous price movements that are not source errors; distinguishing them from corrupted data requires context outside the scope of this service.
